name: Emergency Medicine
tag: Hourly/shift/RVU pay, nights, acuity, boarding, APP supervision, throughput metrics, group stability.
questions: Is pay hourly, RVU, or hybrid?
Are APPs supervised and is supervision paid?

samples.name: Hospital-Employed ED
samples.pros: Stable benefits and direct hospital alignment.
samples.cons: Boarding, APP supervision, metrics, and schedule burden need detail.

samples.name: Democratic EM Group
samples.cons: Hospital contract loss, tail, and nights/weekends must be reviewed.

samples.name: Locums/1099 EM Role
samples.cons: No benefits, travel, malpractice/tail, and schedule instability.

Compensation: Is pay hourly, RVU-based, shift-based, salary, or hybrid?
What are the day, evening, night, weekend, holiday, and backup rates?
Are RVUs paid on top of hourly or included?
Are extra shifts, surge shifts, retention, sign-on, relocation, or loan repayment paid?
Are there clawbacks if I leave early?
Clinical model: What is expected patients/hour by shift and site?
What is acuity mix, admission rate, pediatric volume, trauma designation, and critical-care burden?
How bad is boarding, psych holding, transfer delay, and hallway medicine?
What specialist backup is available and actually responsive?
Are scribes, strong nursing, ultrasound, airway support, and procedure supplies available?
APP supervision: How many APPs are supervised per shift?
Is APP supervision compensated separately? hourly stipend, RVU share, chart fee, or built into rate?
Who signs APP charts and owns liability?
Are APPs independent fast-track clinicians or do they require real-time attending involvement?
Is APP productivity counted toward physician, APP, or group?
Quality bonus: Are bonuses tied to door-to-doc, LWBS, patient satisfaction, sepsis/stroke/STEMI metrics, documentation, throughput, or admission decisions?
What is max quality bonus and historical average payout?
Are metrics physician-controllable or mostly hospital/system dependent?
Can metrics reduce compensation or only add upside?
Lifestyle / schedule: How many nights, weekends, holidays, and swing shifts are required?
Is scheduling democratic, seniority-based, random, or controlled by leadership?
Can shifts be reduced without losing benefits?
How far in advance is the schedule released?
Group / contract risk: Is this hospital-employed, CMG, democratic group, academic, locums, or private contract group?
Is partnership available? timeline, buy-in, distribution, voting rights?
Can the hospital contract be lost and what happens to clinicians if it changes?
Claims-made or occurrence malpractice, and who pays tail?
Are there noncompetes, nonsolicits, or restrictive covenants?

Clinical Fit: Acuity, trauma level, boarding, psych holds, and specialist backup match comfort level.
Compensation Upside: Hourly/RVU/hybrid pay, nights/weekends/holidays, APP supervision, and extra shifts are quantified.
Lifestyle Fit: Nights, weekends, holidays, schedule control, and recovery time are sustainable.
Risk Safety: Tail, contractor status, hospital contract loss, noncompete, and clawbacks are acceptable.
Strategic Fit: Group governance, leadership, medical director path, and site stability build value.
Collaborative Fit: Nursing, APPs, scribes, consultants, hospitalists, and administrators are responsive.
